title: Scheduled flows: record a run whose time passed while the hosted kernel was not ticking as missed, visible in the run history (no replay)
body:
Filing gate ②: from the maintainer's ruling on objectstack-ai/cloud#3149 (batch #386 item 5, item 5). Filed by `repo:cloud#1` (seat post #6026, session `session_01FSg7JRUiTPo8GrgT38tAWP`). ⛔ Not a claim.

**Reader who acts:** the objectstack lane. objectstack-ai/cloud#3149 (the tracker) is `Blocked-by:` this card.

## The gap (cloud#3149 item 5)
- `packages/service-ai-studio/src/verify/clock-trigger-arming.ts` (cloud) records that an armed hosted kernel does not tick until the environment is next opened after a restart or eviction.
- A scheduled run whose time passed in that gap is neither replayed nor recorded, so an app cannot tell a sweep did not run.

## The ruling (what binds)
- **Record only:** on the next tick, each scheduled flow whose due time passed while the kernel was not ticking gets one run-history entry with status `missed` (due time, detected time).
- ⛔ **No replay.**
- objectstack-ai/cloud#1288 (the control-plane clock) is **not** restarted by this ruling.

## Acceptance
- A kernel stopped across one due time of a scheduled flow, then started, shows one `missed` entry for that due time in the flow's run history, and runs nothing for it.
- A kernel that ticked through shows no `missed` entry.
